chunks: Today will depart with all that it has, and tomorrow will come in its wake.
It is as though every one of you has reached that place on earth where he would be alone, namely the location of his grave.
So, what to say of the lonely house, the solitary place of staying and the solitary exile.
It is as though the cry (of the Horn) has reached you, the Hour has overtaken you and you have come out (of your graves) for the passing of judgement.
(The curtains of) falsehood have been removed from you and your excuses have become weak. The truth about you has been proved. All your matters have proceeded to their consequences.
Therefore, you should (now) take counsel from examples, learn lessons from vicissitudes and take advantage of the warners.

key_terms.الصَّيْحَةُ: The cry of the Horn signaling the end of the world
key_terms.الْعِبَرُ: Lessons or examples taken from events
key_terms.الْغُرْبَة: Exile or strangeness, referring to the soul's state in the grave
key_terms.فَصْلِ الْقَضَاءِ: The passing of judgement / separation of deeds

ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about the transition from life to the grave and the importance of learning from signs?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) employs vivid imagery of the grave as a 'house of solitude' to illustrate the individual's ultimate accountability after the collective distractions of worldly life have vanished. This passage, characteristic of the 'Urging towards Piety' sermons, emphasizes the transition from the temporal realm to the eternal reality of judgment, urging believers to internalize these warnings before the 'cry' of death severs all ties. It serves as a profound reminder that truth will eventually manifest from its concealed state, making this a critical moment for spiritual preparation.
